title: Fixing shared randomness preserves communication complexity
statement: Let $p$ be a public-coin communication protocol over a shared randomness space $\Omega$, with Alice's private input in $X$, Bob's in $Y$, and output in $\alpha$, and let $\omega \in \Omega$ be any outcome of the shared randomness. Then the communication complexity of the deterministic protocol obtained from $p$ by fixing the shared randomness to $\omega$ equals the communication complexity of $p$ itself.
hypotheses_covered: p is a public-coin protocol over randomness space Ω with inputs in X and Y and output in α
ω is an element of Ω
replaced:
Fixing the shared randomness does not change the communication complexity:
$(p.\mathrm{toDeterministic}\,\omega).\mathrm{complexity} = p.\mathrm{complexity}$
for every $\omega : \Omega$.
